utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for today starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, Barney Thomas, Rafael La Cruz, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Perisic's Defence will today be represented by Tina Drolec and Milos Androvic, our assistants; Daniela Tasic, our case manager; and I as his Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. May I just mention that due to some other business that Judge David had to attend to, the Chamber is sitting pursuant to rule 15 bis this afternoon. Good afternoon, Mr. Koster. Just to remind you, sir, that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Koster, good afternoon. Let us continue -- well, I won't be taking much time to cross-examine you today. If you recall, the day before yesterday when we were about to end, I was asking questions about your conversation with General Mladic, and you mentioned the instructions that you had received from your operation centre, that you were to relay to Mladic the message to contact your superior, Mr. Karremans. My first question to you is, did you hear whether the two of them actually got in contact? Did you receive any feedback about their contacts, if any?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I chose to stay in my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness had said a lot more than just that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the witness please repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you please repeat yourself, Mr. Koster, I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. In answer to your question, I told to General Mladic that he should contact my commander. He chose not to do so, and he stayed with me, so I do not know whether maybe they had contact afterwards. But at the time when he was with me, they had no contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the following days, did Mr. Karremans go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Commander Karremans did at a certain moment come to my position, but General Mladic was not at my position at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The same day when you yourself had this encounter with Mladic, first encounter?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No, no. He was not at my position, Karremans. They did not have contact at my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. My question is only whether on that day when you had the first encounter with Mr. Mladic and when you relayed to him this message that he should contact Karremans, whether on that day Karremans came to Potocari later on once Mladic had left?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Karremans, Commander Karremans, at a certain time came to my location, but I do not remember whether that was the same day or the day after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so that I follow, is it not so, Mr. Koster, that Mr. Karremans was in the same compound with you at Potocari but in a different building from where you were with Mr. Mladic, or am I misunderstanding something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you say is correct. I was outside the compound with the refugees, and Mr. Karremans was in the compound, and he was not in my position, not where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And this compound is in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because I wasn't understanding your question when you say did he come to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it was my understanding having read some other transcripts that Mr. Karremans was in Srebrenica at the time, but now we heard from the witness -- well, this is why I actually wanted to ask this question, but now we've cleared that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Koster, you left the enclave of Srebrenica, and you left Potocari on the last convoy; I think it was on the 21st of July. Now, my question, is that so?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Indeed. I left the enclave with the last convoy, but the exact date I cannot remember offhand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, this is not important to me. I want to ask you whether you recall if Colonel Karremans was on the same convoy, whether he left the enclave on the same convoy as you did.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will now show you a segment of the transcript of your evidence in the -- in the proceedings to confirm the indictment against Karadzic and Mladic. That's P383, page 16. Could we please have that up in e-court. You answered some questions that were asked by the Trial Chamber. Could we see the lower part. That's line 25, Judge Odio Beneto asking you questions, and she asked you: [In English] "Had you, your team, ask for help to your superiors or to the superior of command of NATO or UNPROFOR to face this emergency?" [Interpretation] Your response is: [In English] "I did not, no." "Did you receive any additional support for help before or after 11th of July?" And answer is: "No."

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The translation was not complete, so could you please repeat the question. That may be difficult, maybe, but please do repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the transcript in front of you, starting with line 26 in the English language. [In English] "Had you, your team, asked for help to your superiors or to the superior command or NATO or UNPROFOR to face this emergency? Answer: "I did not, no. No." "Did you receive any additional support for help before or after 11th of July?" Answer: "No."

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I do remember that I said that, yes, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to ask the question. In fact, I merely wanted to first show this part of the transcript to the witness. My question is: Do you recall if any of your superiors, Karremans or whoever, from your unit tell you that at that time, in the period after the 11th, that any intervention was sought from NATO or UNPROFOR regarding the situation that ensued after the 11th of July, and I'm referring in particular to the huge number of refugees that showed up at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I do not remember. At that time, I was very busy handling the situation at my position, and I do not recall whether I had contact with my superiors about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question is not whether you had contact with your superiors. The question is: "Do you recall if any of your superiors, Karremans or whoever from your unit, told you" -- or "tell you that at that time, in the period after the 11th, that any intervention was sought from NATO or UNPROFOR regarding the situation..." Did Karremans give you any report about any help that he sought from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember that at this time, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, I'll ask you something about another topic, and it concerns your testimony and some of the documents admitted into evidence. You described how on the 13th in the afternoon, you heard that near the base there were about nine corpses, and you then went there with your colleague Mr. Van Shaik. Do you remember where you were when you heard these rumours, when this information reached you.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, the information reached me in two different ways. I heard about this when I was at the compound, and I subsequently heard about it when I was at my position with the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were told this by the refugees or your colleagues from your unit?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I remember that the contact at the compound was with my colleagues, and they told me over there that there were rumours about that, but I don't know for certain, when I was back at my position with the refugees outside the compound, I don't know whether I heard that from the refugees as well as from my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You remained at the base in Potocari until the last part of the convoy left, and in your previous testimony you mentioned the date of the 21st of July. My question is the following: When was the evacuation of civilians completed? When were all the civilians taken away from the base in Potocari? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, I have a question for clarification purposes. Do you mean the refugees who were out of the compound or all refugees who were at the compound?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mean both. The refugees, that is.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Thank you. The refugees outside the compound, I remember that was on the 13th. It happened on the 13th. At the time I went back to the compound and when I wanted to make my way back to my position outside the compound, I was told that the refugees had already been evacuated. As far as the refugees at the compound were concerned, I can't say with absolute certainty on what day the last ones left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us that in relation to the time when you left, did you remain at the base on your own for a few days after the refugees left in?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that there was a group of wounded who were evacuated after the refugees left and that some international organisations were present at their evacuation?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the large group is evacuated, the group that was outside the base on the 13th of July, you went back to your regular tasks, that is, your preparations to leave the enclave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until you left the enclave definitely, did you continue to have the kind of daily briefings you had had before these events?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were issued every day. I was informed about the state of affairs, but I don't know whether that happened every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say you were informed, I assume you had some sort of meeting where the officers gathered and received information. That's my understanding of the word "briefing."

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, but I cannot tell you whether that happened every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But did it happen in that manner? Did you get the briefing in the form of a group of officers being briefed by somebody else, maybe a superior, or did you get informed by written notes to wherever you were? I thought that was the gravamen of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I request that the -- I would like to clarify the answer. Information was distributed in the format of a briefing, as you meant, but also orally. I can't tell you how many times I was given a briefing or how many times I was simply in oral contact with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before these events, you had briefing meetings twice a day, in the morning and in the afternoon, regular meetings of the officers in your unit. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At these meetings, information that officers had obtained was exchanged, and the superiors gave you tasks and told you what to do next.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your stay in the enclave after these events until the time you left the enclave definitely with the last group of convoys of members of your unit, you heard of no massacres, murders, or other crimes on the territory of Potocari, Srebrenica, and the entire enclave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: During that period, there were various rumours that circulated, but I did not receive official reports during a briefing apart from my own perception of the nine dead that I found.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have part of P383, page 17, on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You answered Judge Beneto's questions here, and it's line 16. I'll read it in English. [In English] "Did you hear about massacre committed by Serb soldiers, again, Muslims, in around Srebrenica, Potocari, Bratunac at that time?" "No, I only learned on Wednesday that there were position, there were rumours about eight or nine bodies." "After those days have you heard about massacre committed?" "No, only when I returned in the news." [Interpretation] My question is the following: When you say when "I returned in the news," do you mean when you returned to the Netherlands? Did you hear it in the news there?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon again, Colonel. Colonel, you were asked on Tuesday by my learned friend at page 22554, Your Honours, of the transcript at line 18, you were asked if whether in the course of your meeting with General Mladic you had any reason to suspect that he would not be taking the refugees to a safe territory; and as part of your answer to that question, you said that there was cause for you to doubt the certainty that he would, indeed, relocate them in a proper manner. Do you remember the questions that you were asked on Tuesday about this issue?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Colonel, did you or any other members of DutchBat do anything about those concerns that you had?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We expressed those concerns, and ultimately we were able to turn those into action when the male were separated from the female refugees. We tried to get as many men as possible onto the buses and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Get as many -- which men? Sorry, which men on the buses and trucks?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: In this case, the men who were selected by the Bosnian Serb soldiers from the refugees, we tried to get them on the buses and trucks after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And how would you do that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: It was tricky because we needed to use oral tactics and use arguments to wrest people free from the Bosnian Serb soldiers and to pull them away from them, to get them -- to propel them in the direction of the mass of refugees, and sometimes that worked, but other times the men were dragged along, anyway, and taken away in the direction of the white house, so it was very tricky.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What sort of arguments would you use?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: In my case, it was a bit easier for my fellow members of the military because I was able to invoke my rank and state that I objected to the men being taken away, and sometimes I was able to voice that in more forceful terms, and the Bosnian Serb soldiers responded to that, and then I would use the doubt on the part of the Bosnian Serb soldiers to take the younger men and the more elderly men away and, in the confusion, to propel them toward the buses. We tried to indicate that we objected to the men being separated from the women.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you or other DutchBat soldiers have concerns for the people already on the buses?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, in two ways. One was, what is going to happen to these people and where they were headed, because it was unclear to us where they would be taken, and in which direction; and B, what would happen to them? We had no idea. We hadn't been told, so we were concerned about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you or other DutchBat officers do anything about that concern?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We tried basically on every bus or truck to place at least one DutchBat serviceman so that we had a clear view and some control over where the refugees were going and what would happen to them. I believe I remember that we succeeded with one of the first buses, but on the next buses and trucks, my people were sent away.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Who would send them away?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serb servicemen sent them away. They did not agree to DutchBat soldiers accompanying the transport of the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Besides trying to get DutchBat soldiers onto the buses themselves, did you take any other steps?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. In the end, we tried to accompany the refugees in an orderly as manner as possible to the buses, and we tried to stay near the refugees. When they started to leave the position where the refugees were and started walking along the road past the bus, we tried to escort them because at first they were beaten and kicked by the Bosnian Serb servicemen. The refugees were beaten and kicked, so we tried to stop that by standing in between them and trying to be present in as many places as possible to provide some supervision over how the refugees were being evacuated. It was very tricky because we had very few people on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Once buses were loaded up and were either preparing to leave or were leaving, did you take any -- or you -- I'm sorry. Did you or any other DutchBat soldiers take any steps at that point?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't completely understand that question. Could you please repeat it one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Once the buses were filled and about to go or had begun to leave, did you or any other DutchBat soldiers take any steps at that point?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. The steps we took included reporting that the buses were setting off on the ops room, and by the ops room they tried to escort the evacuation. One or two jeeps tried to escort it, and we then protested and told the local commander of the Bosnian Serb military on site that they had to wait until we were able to escort the convoy of refugees and could be there, but they did not wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is an ops room? There's something mentioned in your answer, Mr. Koster. It's page 13, line 6, if you look at your screen. It's typed in there but incomplete.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operations room. I mean the operations room, Your Honour. Ops room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, Colonel, whose jeeps were attempting to escort the buses?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [In English] The jeeps from DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And were any of the jeeps able to leave with the buses?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the number of jeeps was very limited, including the people who had to drive the jeeps. There were very few of them. As far as I can remember, they tried, but I'm not sure whether they succeeded. I know that they tried to do so with the first convoy, and with the other convoys, the jeeps were stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The jeeps were blocked by the Bosnian Serb military who did not agree to the jeeps escorting the buses and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the jeeps once they were stopped by the Bosnian Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. All I know is that they were blocked, but I don't know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Colonel, thank you. That's all I have for you. Their Honours might have some questions for you, if you would kindly wait there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Koster, I have a couple of questions for you regarding the corpses you saw. You said that you saw eight or nine of them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was that before the refugees arrived or once they were already with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last, Your Honour, that happened when the refugees were at my location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were they bodies of soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were the bodies of civilians, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have any idea of how they were killed, or was it impossible to know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found these civilians, and they had bullet wounds in their back, so my idea is indeed that they were murdered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any questions arising from the Judge's questions, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one matter by way of clarification in relation to that subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The 92 ter package which has been filed does not contain the previous testimony relating to those nine bodies, and that was not a matter canvassed with Colonel Koster in his direct examination, and the reason for that is because it constitutes one of the agreed facts contained in the filed agreed facts on Srebrenica filed before this Trial Chamber. So I just wanted to alert Your Honours to the reason why it doesn't appear in the package. It's a matter which, as far as the parties are concerned, doesn't require any evidence because it is agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you confirm, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the part of the Defence, there is still the unsolved problem of the last version of the agreed facts and whether or not they are adjudicated facts. We are still discussing this with the OTP. So that this particular incident is, in our view, an adjudicated fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In short, in a very short answer, you do not agree with your learned friend that this is an agreed fact? Okay. It's in the hands of the parties, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I could be heard on that briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is appropriate to be heard on that? Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There is obviously going to be some difficulty, Your Honour, if my learned friends for the Defence wish to now suggest that the -- what is an agreed fact, a filed agreed fact, is no longer an agreed fact. We have witnesses such as Colonel Koster who are being tendered on the basis that they do not need to testify in relation to such matters because they have been agreed. Now, I know my learned friend is wishing to - and there have been discussions about this - to somehow change the status of these agreed facts to ones of adjudicated facts, but at the moment nothing has been advanced in respect of that matter, and so what we are left with is -- are filed agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. Let me cut you short, Mr. Thomas, and I'll tell you why I want to do that. If there are discussions taking place between the parties about whether or not to change the status of those facts, I want to believe that at this stage it is not the intention of the parties to make the Chamber privy to those discussions, and we would like to stay ignorant of those discussions. At this point, the issue is that Judge Picard asked questions, you gave an explanation why you didn't deal with those questions, and your explanation is that it's because these are agreed facts. Your learned friend says, no, they are not agreed facts. The only way to resolve the issue at this point is to say, here is the filing of the agreed facts. What takes place between the parties in an attempt to change that status is still a private matter between the parties, and we don't want to hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour, in which case I simply wish to record that the present position is that these are agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what you say. Your learned friend says something else. We can't take the matter any further at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Except, the record, Your Honour, shows that they are agreed facts. There's a filed joint submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you want to refer to that filed submission, by all means, you can do so, either now or at any other time when it's convenient for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, where I was getting to, Your Honour, is that in the event that the status of the agreed facts changes, the Prosecution reserves the right to recall Colonel Koster if the issue, for example, of the nine bodies is going to become contested, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough, and I'm sure you'll raise that with your learned friend in your private discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do you have any questions to the witness arising from the questions by the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Koster, thank you very much. This brings us to the end of your testimony, and we just want to say thank you for coming to testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down, and please travel well back home. I know you don't have far to go. You are home already, but still, it's snowing outside. Travel well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With no other witnesses scheduled to give testimony today, Your Honours, that concludes what we can usefully assist you with. I understand from the Registry, however, that there might be some procedural matters that Your Honours wish to raise at the conclusion of Colonel Koster's testimony today, or that was the message that we received earlier in the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I seem to remember having said that, but at this point in time I must confess, I don't remember what it was that was to be raised. It will be raised in due course when it is remembered. Thank you so much. You want to stand, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only remind Your Honours that the Defence was to state its position on the three questions of the Chamber concerning 98 bis. We have filed a written response, so there is probably no need for us to state our position orally now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The three issues, what are you talking about? Are you talking about site visits, 98 bis, and what have you? Are those the three issues you are talking about? Yes, I guess the Chamber will come back to the parties on that. That being the case, I don't think there's anything else to raise. Then we'll have to adjourn until next week on Tuesday the 9th at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of December, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24

procedural_notes.text: WITNESS:  EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.58 p.m.,
